acme_integration: Hi team — after our deploy yesterday our embedding vectors changed shape. downstream rejects them (expected 1536). samples show length 1024. no code change on our side, just rotated keys. anyone seen this?

anna_support: sorry to hear that. can you paste the request (headers + body) or a minimal curl that reproduces? also which model id you expect?

acme_integration: we expect embed-large-1536 (old contract). here's a redacted curl we used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_proj_public_XXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input": "test text"}'
```

anna_support: thanks. two quick checks: 1) are you passing an org header (we use that to pick org-scoped model routing when token is project-scoped)? 2) can you share full response metadata (model field if present, dims)

acme_integration: no org header set in that curl. response looks like: 
```json
{"data": [{"object": "embedding", "embedding": [/* 1024 floats */], "model": "embed-medium-1024"}], "usage": {...}}
```

anna_support: OK that explains it. if you use a project token that belongs to a different org or a legacy project token the routing can fall back to a default model for that token's org. that default for your token is embed-medium-1024.

jordan_eng: adding: our routing precedence is: 1) explicit Org header (Redwood-Org) 2) project-scoped token mapping 3) account default. If the request lacked Redwood-Org and the token maps to another project, it will route to that project's default embedding model — hence 1024 dims.

acme_integration: ugh. so this is an auth/project misconfig. will adding Redwood-Org header be safe for us?

jordan_eng: yes — set header to the org id that owns the expected model. Example: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_proj_public_XXX" \n  -H "Redwood-Org: org_acme_123" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input": "test text", "model": "embed-large-1536"}'
```
This forces routing to your org and the embed-large-1536 model. Also you can include explicit model param to double-ensure selection.

mike_sre: quick note on batching/throughput — if you switched models you'll see different per-token costs and perf. embed-large-1536 has larger vector size and slightly higher latency. watch batch_size and request concurrency.

carlos_billing: ping — we saw unexpected increase in token ops billed to the org linked to that token. looks like some requests went to the other org's embed-medium-1024 which has different billing. if you want us to reassign charges we can investigate but we'll need request ids + timestamps.

acme_integration: thanks — we patched the header in our integration and tests show 1536 vectors again. sample response: 
```json
{"data": [{"object":"embedding","embedding":[/* 1536 floats */],"model":"embed-large-1536"}], "usage": {...}}
```
Looks good.

anna_support: great! steps we'll recommend in the ticket: 1) prefer org-scoped API keys when multi-org setup isn't required; 2) always set Redwood-Org header for explicit routing when using shared/project tokens; 3) validate embedding dimension in smoke tests after key rotations; 4) add a small alert if embedding dims != expected.

acme_integration: will do. appreciate the quick turnaround :tada:

deploy-bot: Deployed config change to acme-integration service (env var REDWOOD_ORG set).

mike_sre: leaving one follow-up: we saw a handful of requests still coming from an IP that maps to the old CI job (no header). recommend rotating that project token or adding the header there, otherwise routing will keep hitting the other org's defaults.

acme_integration: noted, rotating tokens now. thanks all.

carlos_billing: if you DM me the invoice ids I can flag the charge while we sort reconcilliation.

anna_support: closing the thread after you confirm billing vs routing resolved. feel free to reopen if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
